title: Get the ball rolling
details:
Example: Let’s get the ball rolling with introductions.

Usage: Conversational; initiate shared work.

title: Keep me in the loop
details:
Example: Keep me in the loop about the project.

Usage: Informal workplace usage; request updates.

title: Be on the same page
details:
Example: Let’s check we’re on the same page.

Usage: Conversational; align expectations.

title: Meet the deadline
details:
Example: We need another day to meet the deadline.

Usage: Neutral; complete work on time.

title: Take on board
description: Consider and accept feedback or ideas.
details:
Example: I’ll take your comments on board.

Usage: Neutral; often used when receiving feedback.

title: Get up to speed
description: Learn enough to become fully informed.
details:
Example: I need a day to get up to speed.

Usage: Conversational; learn current details or processes.

title: Work out the details
details:
Example: We’ll work out the details tomorrow.

Usage: Neutral; plan practical specifics.

title: Raise a concern
details:
Example: Can I raise a concern about the budget?

Usage: Neutral to formal; flag an issue politely.

title: Put forward an idea
details:
Example: She put forward an idea at the meeting.

Usage: Neutral; propose a possible approach.

title: Follow up on
description: Take further action about an earlier matter.
details:
Example: I’ll follow up on your email tomorrow.

Usage: Neutral; continue an earlier discussion or task.

title: Hand in
details:
Example: Please hand in your essay by Friday.

Usage: Neutral; common in education.

title: Fall behind
details:
Example: I fell behind with my reading.

Usage: Neutral; often followed by with or on.

title: Stay on top of
details:
Example: I use a list to stay on top of deadlines.

Usage: Conversational; maintain control of tasks.

title: Learn the ropes
description: Learn how a job or activity works.
details:
Example: It took a week to learn the ropes.

Usage: Informal; learn practical basics.

title: A steep learning curve
description: A period requiring rapid, substantial learning.
details:
Example: My first month was a steep learning curve.

Usage: Neutral; common idiomatic workplace meaning.

title: Think outside the box
details:
Example: We need to think outside the box here.

Usage: Conversational workplace expression; can sound clichéd.

title: Go back to the drawing board
description: Restart planning after an unsuccessful attempt.
details:
Example: The trial failed, so it’s back to the drawing board.

Usage: Conversational; rethink a plan fundamentally.

title: Pull your weight
description: Do your fair share of work.
details:
Example: Everyone needs to pull their weight.

Usage: Informal; can sound critical or demanding.

title: On the right track
description: Making progress in the correct direction.
details:
Example: Your first draft is on the right track.

Usage: Neutral; encourage progress.

title: Room for improvement
details:
Example: There’s room for improvement in the introduction.

Usage: Neutral; tactful but clear criticism.
